detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Hydrology - Flood Routing and Flood Control

Return period of rainfall,

$$ T&=50 years

$$p&=$\frac{1}{50}$&=0.02

ce:2013:q10.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 10
ce:2013:q10.question: The pin-jointed 2-D truss is loaded with a horizontal force of 15 kN at joint S and another 15 kN vertical force at joint U, as shown. Find the force in member RS (in kN) and report your answer taking tension as positive and compression as negative. __________

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \Sigma M_{T}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow R_{v} \times 8-15 \times 4+15 \times 4 & =0 \\ \therefore \quad R_{V} & =0\\ \text{Take moment about V, } M_{V}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad R_{H} \times 4&=0 \\ \therefore \quad R_{H}&=0 \end{aligned}$$ We know that if two members meet at a joint which are not collinear and also there is no external forces acting on that joint then both members will carry zero forces. $\therefore F_{O V}=F_{Q R}=0$ Now, consider joint R , $\Sigma F_{y}=0$ $$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow F_{R U} \sin 45^{\circ}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow F_{R U}&=0\\ \text{Now},\quad \Sigma F_{x}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad F_{R S}+F_{R U} \cos 45^{\circ}&=0 \\ \therefore F_{R S}&=0 \end{aligned}$$ So, force is member is "RS" will be zero. Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2013:q12.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 12
ce:2013:q12.question:
In its natural condition, a soil sample has a mass of 1.980 kg and a volume of 0.001 $m^{3}$. After being completely dried in an oven, the mass of the sample is 1.800 kg. Specific gravity G is 2.7. 
Unit weight of water is 10 kN/$m^{3}$. The degree of saturation of the soil is:

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \rho &=\frac{M}{V} \\ &=\frac{1.980}{0.001}=1980 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \rho_{d} &=\frac{M_{d}}{V}\\ &=\frac{1.800}{0.001}=1800 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \rho_{d} &=\frac{\rho}{1+\mathrm{w}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1800 &=\frac{1980}{1+\mathrm{w}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \mathrm{w}=0.1 \\ \because \quad & \rho_{\mathrm{d}}=\frac{\mathrm{G} \cdot \rho_{\mathrm{w}}}{1+\mathrm{e}}\\ \Rightarrow \quad 1800&=\frac{2.7 \times 1000}{1+e} \\ \Rightarrow \quad e&=0.5 \\ \because wG&=e.s\\ \Rightarrow 0.1 \times 2.7&=0.5 S \\ \Rightarrow \quad S&=0.54 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2013:q23.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 23
ce:2013:q23.question:
It was observed that 150 vehicles crossed a particular location of a highway ina duration of 30
minutes. Assuming that vehicle arrival follows a negative exponential distribution, find out the
number of time headways greater than 5 seconds in the above observation? __________

detailed_solution.markdown:
$P(x)=\frac{\lambda^{n} e^{-\lambda}}{x !}$

Where, P(x) is the probability of x events (vehicle arrivals) in some time interval (t).

$\lambda$ is the mean arrival rate in that interval.

$\lambda=\frac{150}{30 \times 60} \times 5=\frac{5}{12}$

Now, the probability that zero vehicle arrive in an interval t, denoted as P(0), will be same as the probability that the headway (into arrival time) greater than or equal to t.

$$\begin{array}{l} \therefore P(x=0)=\frac{\lambda^{0} e^{-\lambda}}{0 !}=e^{-5 / 12}=0.6592 \\ \therefore P(x=0)=0.6592 \end{array}$$

Number of time headway in 30 minutes

$$\begin{array}{l} =0.6592 \times 30 \times 60 \\ =1186.63 \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2013:q26.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 26

The state of 2D-stress at a point is given by the following matrix of stresses:

$$\begin{aligned} \sigma_{1 / 2} &=\frac{\sigma_{x}+\sigma_{y}}{2} \pm \sqrt{\left(\frac{\sigma_{x}-\sigma_{y}}{2}\right)^{2}+\tau_{x y}^{2}} \\ &=\frac{100+20}{2} \pm \sqrt{\left(\frac{100-20}{2}\right)^{2}+(30)^{2}} \\ &=60 \pm 50 \\ \sigma_{1} &=110 ; \sigma_{2}=10 \\ \therefore \tau_{\max } &=\frac{\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{2}}{2}=\frac{110-10}{2}=50 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2013:q27.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 27
ce:2013:q27.question:
Find the magnitude of the error (correct to two decimal places) in the estimation of following integral using Simpson's $\frac{1}{3}$ Rule. Take the step length as 1. __________

$\int_{0}^{4}(x^{4}+10)dx$

detailed_solution.markdown: Using Simpson's Rule, $$\begin{aligned} & \int_{0}^{4}\left ( x^{4}+10 \right )dx \\ &=\frac{1}{3}\left [ \left ( 10+266 \right )+2\left ( 26 \right )+4\left ( 11+91 \right ) \right ] \\ &=245.33 \\ &\text{The value of integral,} \\ \int_{0}^{4}\left ( x^{4}+10 \right )dx&=\left [ \frac{x^{5}}{5}+10x \right ]^{4}_{0} \\ &=\frac{4^{5}}{5}+10\times 4 \\ &=244.8 \\ \therefore \; &\text{ MAgnitude of error}\\ &=245.33-244.8 \\ &=0.53\end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2013:q29.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 29
ce:2013:q29.question:
Find the value of $\lambda$ such that the function f(x) is a valid probability density function. __________
$$\begin{aligned} f(x)&=\lambda (x-1)(2-x)& for \; 1\leq x\leq 2\\ &=0& otherwise \end{aligned}$$

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \int_{-\infty }^{\infty }f\left ( x \right )dx&=1 \\ f\left ( x \right )=\left \{ \begin{matrix} \lambda \left ( -x^{2}+3x-2 \right ) & 1\leq x\leq 2\\ 0 & otherwise \end{matrix} \right. &\\ \therefore\;\;  \int_{1}^{2}\lambda \left ( -x^{2}+3x-2 \right )dx&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \lambda \left [ -\frac{x^{3}}{3}+3\frac{x^{2}}{2}-2x \right ]_{1}^{2}&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \lambda \left [ -\left ( \frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{3} \right )+\frac{3}{2}\left ( 4-1 \right )-2\left ( 2-1 \right ) \right ]&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \lambda \left [ -\frac{7}{3}+\frac{9}{2}-2 \right ]&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \lambda \left [ \frac{-14+27-12}{6} \right ]&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \lambda &=\frac{6}{1}=6 \\   \lambda &=6 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2013:q30.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 30
ce:2013:q30.question:
Laplace equation for water flow in soils is given below.
$\frac{\partial^2 H}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 H}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2 H}{\partial z^2}=0$
Head H does not vary in y and z directions.
Boundary conditions are: at x = 0, H = 5; and $\frac{dH}{dx}=-1$.
What is the value of $H$ at $x = 1.2$? __________

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\frac{\partial^{2} H}{\partial x^{2}}=0$

Integrating both sides, we get

$\frac{\partial H}{\partial x}=C_{1} \quad \ldots(i)$

Integrating again

$$\begin{aligned} H&=C_{1} x+C_{2}\\ \text{At }\quad x&=0, H=5 \\ \therefore \quad 5&=C_{2} \\ \text{At }\quad x&=0, \frac{d H}{d x}=-1 \end{aligned}$$

From eq. (i)

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore C_{1}&=-1 \\ \therefore \quad H&=-x+5 \\ \text { At } x &=1.2 \mathrm{m} \\ \therefore \quad \mathrm{H}&=5-1.2=3.8 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2013:q32.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 32
ce:2013:q32.question: A uniform beam (EI=constant) PQ in the form of a quarter-circle of radius R is fixed at end P and free at the end Q, where a load W is applied as shown. The vertical downward displacement, $\delta _{q}$, at the loaded point Q is given by: $\delta _{q}=\beta (\frac{WR^{3}}{EI})$. Find the value of $\beta$(correct to 4-decimal places). __________

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} U &=\int \frac{M^{2} d x}{2 E l}=\int_{0}^{\pi / 2} \frac{(W R \sin \theta)^{2} R d \theta}{2 E l} \\ &=\int_{0}^{\pi / 2} \frac{P^{2} R^{3}}{2 E l} \sin ^{2} \theta d \theta \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} &=\frac{P^{2} R^{3}}{2 E I} \int_{0}^{\pi / 2} \frac{(1-\cos 2 \theta) d \theta}{2} \\ &=\frac{P^{2} R^{3}}{4 E I}\left[\theta-\frac{\sin 2 \theta}{2}\right]_{0}^{\pi / 2} \\ &=\frac{P^{2} R^{3}}{4 E I}\left[\frac{\pi}{2}\right]=\frac{P^{2} R^{3} \pi}{8 E I} \\ \therefore \quad \delta_{Q}&=\frac{\partial U}{\partial W}=\frac{2 P R^{3} \pi}{8 E I}=\frac{P R^{3}}{E I} \frac{\pi}{4} \\ \therefore \quad \delta_{Q}&=\frac{\pi}{4}\left(\frac{W R^{3}}{E !}\right) \\ \therefore \quad \beta&=\frac{\pi}{4}=0.7854 \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

(i) $$\begin{aligned} T_{A B} \times 0.8575 &=1125 \\ T_{A B} &=1311.96 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

A rectangular concrete beam 250mm wide and 600mm deep is pre-stressed by means of 16 high

bending moment (in kNm) (correct to 1-decimal place) due to live load that this section of the beam
can with stand without causing tensile stress at the bottom face of the beam? Neglect the effect of dead load of beam.

detailed_solution.markdown: since the tensile stress at bottom face of the beam is zero. $$\begin{aligned} \frac{P}{A}+\frac{P e}{I} y-\frac{M}{I} y &=0 \\ P &=700 \times \frac{\pi}{4}(7)^{2} \times 16 \\ &=431.026 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}$$ since the prestressing force is located at 200 mm from the bottom face of the beam. $\therefore$ Eccentricity $=300-200=100 \mathrm{mm}$ $$\begin{array}{l} \frac{431.03 \times 10^{3}}{250 \times 600}+\frac{431.03 \times 10^{3} \times 100}{250 \times 600^{2}} \times 6 \\ =\frac{M \times 6}{250 \times 600^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow 2.87+2.87=6.66 \times 10^{-8} M \\ \Rightarrow M=86.205 \mathrm{kNm} \end{array}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2013:q36.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 36
ce:2013:q36.question: The soil profile below a lake with water level at elevation = 0 m and lake bottom at elevation = -10 m is shown in the figure, where k is the permeability coefficient. A piezometer (stand pipe) installed in the sand layer shows a reading of +10 m elevation. Assume that thepiezometric headis uniform in the sand layer. The quantity of water (in $m^{3}$/s) flowing into the lake from the sand layer through the silt layer per unit area of the lake bed is:

detailed_solution.markdown:
From the diagram,

10m of head is lost in 20m of silt layer before reaching lake

$$\begin{aligned} 1 &=\frac{h}{z}=\frac{10}{20}=0.5 \\ Q &=k i A=10^{-6} \times 0.5 \times 1 \\ &=0.5 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2013:q37.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 37
ce:2013:q37.question: The soil profile above the rock surface for a 25$^{\circ}$ infinite slope is shown in the figure, where $s_{u}$ is the undrained shear strength and $\gamma _{t}$ is total unit weight. The slip will occur at a depth of

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Stability Analysis of Slopes
detailed_solution.markdown: The slip will occur when shear stress is greater then or equal to shear strength. $$\begin{aligned} \tau &\geq S_{u} \\ \left(\gamma_{1} z_{1}+\gamma_{2} z_{2}\right) \sin \beta \cos \beta &\geq S_{u}\\ \Rightarrow \frac{\left(16 \times 5+20 \times z_{2}\right) \sin 2 \beta}{2} &\geq S_{u} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\left(80+20 z_{2}\right) \sin 50^{\circ}}{2} &\geq 60 \\ z_{2}&=3.83 \mathrm{m} \\ \text{ Depth of slip }=5+3.83&=8.83 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2013:q38.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 38
ce:2013:q38.question: Two different soil types (Soil 1 and Soil 2) are used as backfill behind a retaining wall as shown in the figure, where $\gamma _{t}$ is total unit weight, and c' and $\phi$' are effective cohesion and effective angle of shearing resistance. The resultant active earth force per unit length (in kN/m) acting on the wall is:

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Retaining Wall-Earth Pressure Theories
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} k_{a 1} &=\frac{1-\sin 30^{\circ}}{1+\sin 30^{\circ}}=\frac{1}{3}=0.33 \\ k_{a_{2}} &=\frac{1-\sin 40^{\circ}}{1+\sin 40^{\circ}}=0.217 \\ P_{a_{1}} &=\frac{1}{2} k_{a_{1}} \gamma_{1} H_{1}^{2}=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{3} \times 15 \times 2^{2} \\ &=10 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} P_{a_{2}} &=k_{a_{2}} \gamma_{1} H_{1} \cdot H_{2}=0.217 \times 15 \times 2 \times 2 \\ &=13.02 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} \\ P_{a_{3}} &=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{k}_{02} \gamma_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}^{2}=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.217 \times 20 \times 2^{2} \\ &=8.68 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} \\ P_{a} &=P_{a_{1}}+P_{\mathrm{a}_{2}}+P_{a_{3}}=10+13.02+8.68 \\ P_{\mathrm{a}} &=31.7 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2013:q39.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 39
ce:2013:q39.question:
A 2 km long pipe of 0.2 m diameter connects two reservoirs. The difference between water levels
in the reservoirs is 8 m. The Darcy-Weisbachfriction factor of the pipe is 0.04. Accounting for
frictional, entry and exit losses, the velocity in the pipe (in m/s) is:

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Flow Through Pipes
detailed_solution.markdown:
Frictional loss,

$n_{1}=\frac{1 L V^{2}}{d \times 20}$

Loss of head at entrance,

$h_{L}=\frac{0.5 V^{2}}{2 g}$

Loss at exit of pipe.

$$\begin{aligned} h_{c}&=\frac{V^{2}}{2g}\\ \therefore 8 &= \frac{fLV^{2}}{d\times }+\frac{0.5V^{2}}{2g}+\frac{V^{2}}{2g}\\ \Rightarrow \quad 8 &= \frac{0.04\times 2000\times V^{2}}{2\times g\times 0.2}+\frac{V^{2}}{2g}+\frac{0.5V^{2}}{2g}\\ \Rightarrow\quad 8&=20.3873V^{2}+0.07645V^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad V&=0.625 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ &= 0.63 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2013:q40.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 40
ce:2013:q40.question:
The normal depth in a wide rectangular channel is increased by 10%. The percentage increase in
the discharge in the channel is:

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown:
The discharge in the channel is given by

$$\begin{aligned} Q&=\frac{1}{n} A R^{2 / 3} S^{1 / 2}\\ \Rightarrow \quad Q&=\frac{1}{n}(B y)\left(\frac{B y}{B+2 y}\right)^{2 / 3} S^{1 / 2} \end{aligned}$$

For a wide rectangular channel

$$\begin{aligned} B &\gg y \\ \therefore\quad Q&=\frac{1}{n}(B y)(y)^{2 / 3} S^{1 / 2} \\ \therefore\quad Q &\propto y^{5 / 3} \\ \text{let} Q_{1}&=k(y)^{5 / 3} \\ \therefore\quad Q_{2}&=k(1.1 y)^{5 / 3} \\ \therefore\quad \frac{Q_{2}-Q_{1}}{Q_{1}} \times 100&=\frac{(1.1 \mathrm{y})^{5 / 3}-(\mathrm{y})^{5 / 3}}{(\mathrm{y})^{5 / 3}} \times 100 \\ &= 17.21 \% \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2013:q41.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 41
ce:2013:q41.question:
The transplantation of rice requires 10 days and total depth of water required during transplantation
is 48 cm. During transplantation, there is an effective rainfall (useful for irrigation) of 8 cm. The
duty of irrigation water (in hectares/cumec) is:

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} D &=864 \mathrm{B} / \Delta \mathrm{ha} / \mathrm{cumecs} \\ &=\frac{864 \times 10}{(48-8) \times 10}=216 \mathrm{ha} / \mathrm{cumecs} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2013:q42.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 42
ce:2013:q42.question: A settling tank in a water treatment plant is designed for a surface overflow rate of 30 $\frac{m^{3}}{day\cdot m^{2}}$. Assume specific gravity of sediment particles = 2.65, density of water ($\rho= 1000 kg/m^3$), dynamic viscosity of water ($\mu=0.001 N.s/m^2$), and Stokes' law is valid. The approximate minimum size of particles that would be completely removed is:

detailed_solution.markdown:
To calculate minimum size of particles equating setteling velocity to overflow rate, we get,

$$\begin{aligned} V_{0} &=V_{s} \\ \Rightarrow\; \; V_{0} &=\frac{\left ( G_{s}-1 \right )\gamma _{W}d^{2}}{18\mu } \\ \text{Now }\; \; V_{0}&=\frac{30m^{2}}{day.m^{2}} \\ &=\frac{30}{24\times 60\times 60}\frac{m}{s} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \frac{30}{24\times 60\times 60}&= \frac{\left ( 2.65-1 \right )\times 9.81\times 10^{3}\times d^{2}}{18\times 0.001}\\ \end{aligned}$$

Solving we get,

$d=1.965\times 10^{-5}\; m \approx 0.02\, mm$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2013:q43.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 43
ce:2013:q43.question:
A student began experiment for determination of 5-day, 20$^{\circ}$C BOD on Monday. Since the $5^{th}$ day fell on Saturday, the final DO readings were taken on next Monday. On calculation, BOD (i.e. 7 day, 20$^{\circ}$C) was found to be 150 mg/L. What would be the 5-day, 20$^{\circ}$C BOD (in mg/L)?
Assume value of BOD rate constant (k) at standard temperature of 20$^{\circ}$C as 0.23/day (base e). __________

primary.subtopicLabel: Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} BOD_{7} &=L\left [ 1-e^{-k\times t} \right ] \\ \therefore \; \; 150 &=L\left [ 1-e^{-0.23\times 7} \right ] \\ \Rightarrow \; \; L &=187.54\: mg/L \\ \therefore \; \; BOD_{5} &=L\left [ 1-e^{-k\times t} \right ] \\ &=187.539\times \left [ 1-e^{-0.23\times 5} \right ] \\ &= 128.13\: mg/L \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2013:q46.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 46
ce:2013:q46.question:
Following bearings are observed while traversing with a compass.

After applying the correction due to local attraction, the corrected fore bearing of line BC will be:

detailed_solution.concept: Geomatics Engineering - Theodolites, Compass and Traverse Surveying
detailed_solution.markdown:
The difference between back bearing and fore bearing of line DE

$=258^{\circ} 30^{\circ}-78^{\circ} 30^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$

$\therefore$ Station D and E are free from local attraction

Fore bearing of line $E A=216^{\circ} 30^{\circ}$

$\therefore$ Correct back bearing of line EA

$$\begin{array}{c} =216^{\circ} 30^{\circ}-180^{\circ}=36^{\circ} 30^{\circ}\\ \therefore \text{ Error at } A=31^{\circ} 45^{\circ}-36^{\circ} 30^{\circ} \\ =-4^{\circ} 45^{\circ} \end{array}$$

Hence correction at

$A=+4^{\circ} 45$

$\therefore$ Correct fore bearing of line AB

$$\begin{array}{l} =126^{\circ} 45^{\prime}+4^{\circ} 45^{\prime} \\ =131^{\circ} 30^{\prime} \end{array}$$

Correct back bearing of AB

$$\begin{array}{l} =131^{\circ} 30+180^{\circ} \\ =311^{\circ} 30^{\prime} \end{array}$$

$\therefore$ Error at $B=-3^{\circ} 30^{\circ}$

Correction at $\mathrm{B}=+3^{\circ} 30^{\circ}$

Hence correct bearing of BC

$$\begin{array}{l} =45^{\circ} 15^{\prime}+3^{\circ} 30^{\prime} \\ =48^{\circ} 45^{\prime} \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2013:q47.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 47
ce:2013:q47.question:
A theodolite is set up at station A and a 3 m long staff is held vertically at station B. The depression
angle reading at 2.5 m marking on the staffis 6$^{\circ}$10'. The horizontal distance between A and B is
2200 m. Height of instrument at station A is 1.1 m and R.L. of A is 880.88 m. Apply the curvature
and refraction correction, and determine the R.L. of B (in m). __________

detailed_solution.concept: Geomatics Engineering - Theodolites, Compass and Traverse Surveying
detailed_solution.markdown: RL of $\mathrm{A}=880.88 \mathrm{m}$ RL of plane of collimation $=880.88+1.1=881.98 \mathrm{m}$ $$\begin{aligned} \frac{B B^{\prime \prime}}{C B^{\prime}} &=\tan 6^{\circ} 10^{\prime} \\ B^{\prime} B^{\prime} &=2200 \mathrm{m} \times \tan 6^{\circ} 10^{\prime} \\ &=237.701 \mathrm{m}\\ \text{RL of }B&=R L\text{ of Ine of sight }-B B^{\prime \prime} \\ &=881.98-237.701-(25-0.3257) \\ &=642.105 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2013:q48.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 48
ce:2013:q48.question:
A propped cantilever made of a prismatic steel beam is subjected to a concentrated load P at mid span as shown.

If load P= 80 kN, find the reaction R (in kN) (correct to 1-decimal place) using elastic analysis. __________

detailed_solution.concept: Design of Steel Structures - Plastic Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown: Equating deflection at end B, Let, $l=3m$ $$\begin{aligned} \therefore \; \frac{R\left ( l \right )^{3}}{3EI} &= \frac{P\left ( 1.5 \right )^{3}}{3EI}+\frac{P\left ( 1.5 \right )^{2}}{2EI}\times 1.5 \\ \Rightarrow \; \frac{R\left ( 3 \right )^{3}}{3EI} &= \frac{1.125P}{EI}+\frac{1.6875P}{EI} \\ \frac{9R}{EI} &= \frac{1.125P}{EI}+\frac{1.6875P}{EI} \\ \Rightarrow \; R&=\frac{5}{16}P \\ R&=\frac{5}{16}\times 80=25 kN \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2013:q49.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 49
ce:2013:q49.question:
A propped cantilever made of a prismatic steel beam is subjected to a concentrated load P at mid span as shown.

If the magnitude of load P is increased till collapse and the plastic moment carrying capacity of steel beam section is 90 kNm, determine reaction R (in kN) (correct to 1-decimal place) using plastic analysis. __________

detailed_solution.concept: Design of Steel Structures - Plastic Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} -3M_{P}\theta +P\frac{l}{2}\theta &=0 \\ \therefore \; P_{u}=\frac{6M_{P}}{l}=\frac{6\times 90}{3}&=180\, kN\\ \text{At collapse condition }\sum M_{A}&=0\\ R\times 3+M_{P}-P\times 1.5-M_{P}+M_{P}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \; R&=60 kN \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2013:q50.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 50
ce:2013:q50.question:

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} N &=\left|-\frac{1}{25}-\frac{1}{20}\right|=0.09 \\ S &=0.278 \times 90 \times 2.5+\frac{(90)^{2}}{254 \times 0.35} \\ &=62.55+91.1136=153.6636 \\ \text { Assume } & L>\text { SSD, } \\ L &=\frac{N S^{2}}{(1.50+0.035 S)} \\ \therefore \quad L &=\frac{0.09(153.6636)^{2}}{(1.50+0.035 \times 153.6636)} \\ &=308.9641 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

ce:2013:q52.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 52
ce:2013:q52.question:
A multistory building with a basement is to be constructed. The top 4m consists of loose silt, below which dense sand layer is present up to a great depth. Ground water table is at the surface. The foundation consists of the basement slab of 6 m width which will rest on the top of dense sand as shown in the figure. For dense sand, saturated unit weight = 20kN/$m^3$, and bearing capacity factors $N_q$=40 and $N_{\gamma }$=45. For loose silt, saturated unit weight = 18kN/$m^3$, $N_q$=15 and $N_{\gamma }$=20. Effective cohesion c' is zero for both soils. Unit weight of water is 10 kN/$m^3$. Neglect shape factor and depth factor.

Average elastic modulus E and Poisson's ratio $\mu$ of dense sand is $60 \times 10^3kN/m^2$ and 0.3 respectively.

Using factor of safety = 3, the net safe bearing capacity (in kN/$m^{2}$) of the foundation is:

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Shallow Foundation and Bearing Capacity
detailed_solution.markdown:
As per GATE Official Answer Key MTA (Marks to ALL)

$$\begin{aligned} Q_{u}&=1.3 \mathrm{cN}_{\mathrm{c}}+\left(\gamma^{\prime}\right)_{\mathrm{silt}}\left(\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{q}}\right)_{\mathrm{silt}} \mathrm{D}_{\mathrm{t}}+0.4 \mathrm{B}(\gamma)_{\mathrm{sand}} (N_{\gamma})_{\text{sand}} \\ &=8.19 \times 4 \times 15+0.4 \times 10.19 \times 6 \times 45 \\ &=1591.92 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ & \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{nu}}=\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{u}}-\gamma \mathrm{D}_{\mathrm{f}} \end{aligned}$$

Safe bearing capacity $=Q_{n s}=\frac{Q_{n u}}{F}$

$=\frac{1591.92-8.19 \times 4}{3}=519.72 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2013:q53.title: GATE CE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 53

A multistory building with a basement is to be constructed. The top 4m consists of loose silt, below which dense sand layer is present up to a great depth. Ground water table is at the surface. Effective cohesion c' is zero for both soils. Unit weight of water is 10 kN/$m^3$. Neglect shape factor and depth factor.
